summary.oneLiner: Quarter dominated by an **ongoing Gulf-region crisis (Strait of Hormuz)** that choked Qatar term-LNG supply from March onward — yet Petronet posted its **highest-ever quarterly PBT (INR 1,795 cr) and PAT (INR 1,338 cr)**, aided by a large Use-of-Pay (UOP) reversal and inventory gains. Dahej ran ~90% for the quarter but collapsed to ~53% in March (vs ~108% Jan–Feb). Mgmt frames the disruption as temporary (Qatar supply resumes 3–4 weeks after conflict ends, hoped by June), with structural offsets: capacity expanded 17.5→22.5 mtpa, two new long-term contracts (Exxon, Equinor ~1 mt combined this year), and a multi-year ~INR 9,000 cr/yr capex cycle led by the PDH-PP petrochem project.

thesis: Quarter dominated by an **ongoing Gulf-region crisis (Strait of Hormuz)** that choked Qatar term-LNG supply from March onward — yet Petronet posted its **highest-ever quarterly PBT (INR 1,795 cr) and PAT (INR 1,338 cr)**, aided by a large Use-of-Pay (UOP) reversal and inventory gains. scorecard (yoy where available; one-offs:
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | Q3 FY26 (QoQ) | Q4 FY25 (YoY) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| PBT | INR 1,795 cr | 1,144 cr | 1,446 cr | **Highest-ever**; boosted by UOP reversal |
| PAT (standalone) | INR 1,338 cr | 848 cr | 1,070 cr | **Highest-ever** quarterly PAT |
| Regas revenue (3rd-party) | INR 879 cr | — | — | Reported figure |
| **Total LNG volume** | **219 TBTU** | 233 TBTU | 205 TBTU | YoY +7%; QoQ −6% |
| **Dahej throughput** | **201 TBTU** | 214 TBTU | 189 TBTU | YoY +6%; QoQ −6% |
| **Dahej utilization** | **90.1%** | 93.8% | 85.2% | March cratered to **~53%** (Jan–Feb ~108%) on Qatar supply loss |
| Kochi (FY annual) | 68 TBTU (FY26) | — | — | **Highest-ever annual** Kochi throughput |
| Kochi March util | >20% | — | — | — |
| Net cash / dividend | Final div INR 3/share | — | — | Strong cash; payout maintained in absolute terms |

**FY26 full-year:** PBT INR 5,158 cr / PAT INR 3,843 cr (standalone) vs FY25 PBT 5,275 cr / PAT 3,926 cr — **YoY slightly DOWN**. Consol PAT FY26 INR 3,913 cr vs 3,973 cr.

**Use-or-Pay (CALL OUT):** Customers paid INR 630 cr of outstanding UOP dues for CY2022. Net P&L impact INR ~495–496 cr = INR 550 cr CY22 reversal − INR 35 cr (CY23 provision) − INR 6 cr (CY24 provision) − INR 13 cr (volume-linked waiver). **This is a major one-off inflating Q4 profit.**

**Spot-LNG-price → volume effect (CALL OUT):** Post-crisis spot spiked to ~$25/mmbtu (March spot purchases ~$20), now eased to $15–17. Lower prices are reviving utilization vs March; high March prices suppressed volumes.

**Other one-offs:** Inventory gain INR 95 cr; trading gains INR 118 cr; IndAS Q4 gross-margin +INR 119 cr (FY +629 cr), Q4 FOREX loss INR 91 cr (FY −199 cr).
guidance (critical):
- **Volume/utilization outlook:** Refused a firm FY27 number given Gulf uncertainty. April–May utilization "more or less at the same level as March" (~53% Dahej). Hopeful Qatar supply resumes from **first week of June** (3–4 weeks after conflict ends), reverting to annual delivery plan; talking to Qatar to make good lost volumes within FY27.
- **Tariff hike:** **Kochi regas tariff +5% from April 2026** (constant escalation).
- **PDH-PP / Petchem:** Project "absolutely on track"; equipment sourced from Japan/Korea/China/Europe/US (not Gulf), so unaffected. ~INR 1,650 cr spent in FY26; ~INR 7,500 cr (±10%) budgeted FY27 — the bulk of capex.
- **Capex:** **FY27 ~INR 9,000 cr** (cash basis lower; FY26 cash capex was INR 2,511 cr vs INR 3,000 cr provisioned). FY28 also ~INR 9,000 cr (±10%).
- **New terminals:** Gopalpur terminal construction to start FY27 (~INR 300–400 cr this year, 2 tanks). Third jetty at Dahej (~INR 600 cr). Fifth small-scale LNG plant at Kochi (~INR 70 cr, land acquired).
- **New contracts:** Exxon (new portfolio contract, first cargo April; 0.5 mt) + Equinor via Performance Chemiserve (first cargo 12 May) = ~**1 mt combined incremental this year**.
volume / pipeline:
- Total 219 TBTU (Dahej 201, Kochi balance). March collapse from Qatar supply halt; Jan–Feb ran ~108%.
- Recovery driven by third-party cargoes (GAIL, IOCL, BPCL, GSPC, Torrent) at improved $15–17 spot.
- New supply geographies: Exxon (April first cargo), Oman, Mozambique, Nigeria, Congo, Mauritania, Senegal, Golden Pass (US). India has ~10–12 mt long-term deals signed over last 2–3 years.
- Gujarat Gas guided +5–6 mmscmd demand (Morbi market) from May — potential ~1.5 mtpa (~6–7% of volume) if perpetual.
- Kochi-Bangalore pipeline (GAIL) pushed to ~Sept 2026 / H1 FY27; will lift Kochi utilization once connected to national grid.
segment (dahej / kochi / petrochem):
- **Dahej:** Core engine; 90.1% util Q4, capacity expanded to 22.5 mtpa. Third jetty under construction. Future storage-tank additions planned (land constraint).
- **Kochi:** Record FY26 throughput 68 TBTU; +5% tariff from April; upside from Kochi-Bangalore pipeline + planned additional storage tank (~INR 1,200 cr) + fifth small-scale LNG plant.
- **Petrochem (PDH-PP):** On track, INR 1,650 cr FY26 spend, ~INR 7,500 cr FY27 budget — dominant capex item.
growth / optionality:
- PDH-PP petrochemicals (new earnings vertical, multi-year capex).
- Dahej expansion (17.5→22.5 mtpa) + third jetty; potential ethane storage/handling business models discussed with Deepak group / ONGC.
- New terminals: Gopalpur (2 tanks); Kochi extra tank + 5th small-scale LNG plant.
- Strategic LNG storage build-out (national energy-security theme post-crisis) — tanks at Gopalpur, Kochi, possibly Dahej (3–4 tanks, land pending).
- 2028 SPA back-to-back contract extension under negotiation with offtakers (now DES vs earlier FOB; no incoterm renegotiation seen needed).
margins & cost:
- Regas tariff: Kochi +5% from April (annual escalation); Dahej tariff escalation implied.
- Spot vs term: Term Qatar LNG disrupted; spot ($15–17 now, $20–25 at peak) backfilling. Spot in India linked to JKM / West-India Marker.
- One-offs aiding margin: UOP reversal (~INR 495 cr net), inventory gain (INR 95 cr), trading gains (INR 118 cr), IndAS gross-margin positives.
capex (pdh-pp focus):
- FY27 ~INR 9,000 cr: Petchem/PDH-PP ~INR 7,500 cr (±10%); Gopalpur ~INR 300–400 cr; third jetty ~INR 600 cr; 5th small-scale LNG Kochi ~INR 70 cr; Kochi tank ~INR 1,200 cr (under consideration); routine.
- FY26 cash capex INR 2,511 cr; petchem FY26 ~INR 1,650 cr (incl advances + CWIP).
- Expansion capacity commissioned/capitalized INR 390 cr in Q4, balance ~INR 100 cr in Q1 FY27.
- FY28 also ~INR 9,000 cr.
capital allocation:
- Final dividend INR 3/share for FY26.
- Mgmt: endeavour to **maintain dividend in absolute terms** despite heavy expansion, backed by balance-sheet cash (not payout-% driven).
- Capital advances ~INR 906 cr in non-current assets for ongoing capex.
risks:
- **LNG price → volume sensitivity:** High spot prices (war-driven spikes to $25) suppress utilization (March 53%); recovery hinges on prices/conflict.
- **Gulf/Strait of Hormuz geopolitical risk:** Qatar term supply (core ~8.5 mt) halted; resumption depends entirely on conflict resolution. FY27 visibility low; April–May still depressed.
- **Domestic gas competition:** Capacity holders can route cargoes to other Indian terminals (no control over spot mix at Dahej).
- **PDH-PP execution:** Large multi-year capex; equipment sourcing safe but execution/ramp risk remains.
- **Force-majeure / time-charter:** 3 time-charter vessels (Qatar route) idle during disruption; ~INR 90 cr demand for March disputed as FM (company believes not liable).
mgmt tone: Confident-but-guarded. Repeatedly declined to give FY27 utilization guidance, urging investors to "wait till end of quarter." Optimistic Qatar resumes by June; emphasized record profits and resilience while candid that April–May remain weak ("more or less same as March"). Closing: hopeful Gulf situation improves, "brighter picture" next quarter.
non-obvious:
- Q4 record profit is materially flattered by the **~INR 495 cr UOP reversal one-off** — underlying operating quarter was hit by the supply shock; FY26 full-year PAT actually fell YoY.
- March Dahej at 53% but Jan–Feb at ~108% shows how concentrated the crisis impact was.
- New Exxon contract is a *portfolio* (Gorgon-sourced) deal, distinct from existing 1.42 mt Exxon contract; Equinor flows via Deepak Fertilizers' Performance Chemiserve.
- National energy-security narrative (CEO press conference) is pivoting Petronet toward strategic storage-tank capex — a new structural growth angle.
- Receivables/payables both fell ~INR 2,000 cr YoY simply because Qatar LNG (and matching RLNG sales) didn't flow in March — optical balance-sheet move, not deterioration.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- Gulf supply disruption → spot/portfolio LNG players (Golden Pass/US, Oman, Mozambique, Nigeria, Congo, Mauritania/Senegal) and capacity holders (GAIL, IOCL, BPCL, GSPC) diverting cargoes. ⭐
- National storage-shortfall concern → terminal/storage-tank EPC and Petronet's own tank build-out (Gopalpur, Kochi, Dahej). ✅

Guidance withheld on FY27 utilization pending Qatar supply resumption (~June).

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.

- **PDH-PP execution:** Large multi-year capex; equipment sourcing safe but execution/ramp risk remains.
- **Force-majeure / time-charter:** 3 time-charter vessels (Qatar route) idle during disruption; ~INR 90 cr demand for March disputed as FM (company believes not liable).

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious
non_obvious.body:
- Q4 record profit is materially flattered by the **~INR 495 cr UOP reversal one-off** — underlying operating quarter was hit by the supply shock; FY26 full-year PAT actually fell YoY.
- March Dahej at 53% but Jan–Feb at ~108% shows how concentrated the crisis impact was.
- New Exxon contract is a *portfolio* (Gorgon-sourced) deal, distinct from existing 1.42 mt Exxon contract; Equinor flows via Deepak Fertilizers' Performance Chemiserve.
- National energy-security narrative (CEO press conference) is pivoting Petronet toward strategic storage-tank capex — a new structural growth angle.
- Receivables/payables both fell ~INR 2,000 cr YoY simply because Qatar LNG (and matching RLNG sales) didn't flow in March — optical balance-sheet move, not deterioration.

challenges.title: Challenges → Beneficiaries
challenges.body:
- Gulf supply disruption → spot/portfolio LNG players (Golden Pass/US, Oman, Mozambique, Nigeria, Congo, Mauritania/Senegal) and capacity holders (GAIL, IOCL, BPCL, GSPC) diverting cargoes. ⭐
- National storage-shortfall concern → terminal/storage-tank EPC and Petronet's own tank build-out (Gopalpur, Kochi, Dahej). ✅

---

qoq_log.title: QoQ Log
qoq_log.body: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Record PBT/PAT but flattered by UOP reversal; Dahej 90.1% (March 53% on Gulf crisis); Kochi record FY annual 68 TBTU; Kochi tariff +5% from April; new Exxon + Equinor contracts (~1 mt); FY27 capex ~INR 9,000 cr (petchem ~7,500 cr); dividend INR 3/share; FY26 PAT slightly down YoY. Guidance withheld on FY27 utilization pending Qatar supply resumption (~June).
